messages:
deploy-bot: Scheduled migration 'rowstamp_normalize' will run 2023-11-15 02:00 UTC in the change window. Preflight -> canary -> gradual backfill. Release notes: https://internal.redwood/release/rowstamp_normalize :rocket:

maria (db): Quick context — this fixes inconsistent rowstamp values that autopopulated from the legacy writer. It's a keyed backfill on users.user_metadata, ~120M rows across tenants, but ~90% small tenants.

kevin: We should avoid an exclusive table lock. Plan: 1) preflight validation read-only check, 2) canary on 5 small tenants, 3) staggered backfill per-tenant with rate limit. No FK churn.

ashley (sre): +1 on staged canary. What's the expected lock footprint for the UPDATE? Need to confirm short txn sizes and no long-lived locks. Also request circuit-breaker on deploy-bot to pause at error rate > 0.5% for 5m.

maria (db): Work plan snippet for preflight check (will run on replica first):

```
-- preflight: detect rows with null/legacy stamps
SELECT count(1) FROM users.user_metadata WHERE rowstamp IS NULL OR rowstamp < '2000-01-01';
```

maria (db): Backfill job will use id-range batching and LIMIT 1000 per txn. Pseudocode:

```
for each tenant_id in target_tenants:
  for id_range in tenant_ranges(tenant_id):
    UPDATE users.user_metadata
    SET rowstamp = coalesce(rowstamp, now())
    WHERE id BETWEEN a AND b
    LIMIT 1000;
    COMMIT;
    sleep(rate_delay);
```

jordan (release): We need to pin the app version for the canary to 2.14.1 so the workers don't pick up the newer writer that emits the legacy stamp. Can we set feature-flag fallback if the migration hits an error?

kevin: I'll create a pin in the deploy manifest: patch below to set canary pin.

```
- name: users-service
  canary: true
  pinned_version: 2.14.1
```

ashley (sre): Ops checklist:
- monitor replica lag < 30s before starting
- enable per-tenant rate cap metric in /observability
- set deploy-bot circuit-break on lock-wait > 2s
- rollback playbook linked: https://internal.redwood/playbooks/migration-rollback

sam (product): Confirmed release notes updated with rollback instructions and user impact (none expected). Notifying CS about scheduled window.

maria (db): Rollback decision rules: if backfill fails more than 3 tenants in a row or avg update latency > 1s for 10m, pause and revert to read-only patch that prevents writer patching. We'll escalate for manual abort if errors persist after 30m.

jordan (release): I'll do the canary gating: 00:00 start preflight, 00:30 canary 5 tenants, 01:30 if healthy start gradual. Tagging rolling window: 02:00-04:00 UTC for wider sweep.

deploy-bot: Canary job created: jobs/rowstamp-canary-1699990000. Will report status here.

deploy-bot: INFO: started preflight checks (replica lag 12s, query sample returned 348 rows needing fix).

kevin: Ack. I'll stand by to increase rate or pause if SLOs change.

ashley (sre): Oncall monitoring hook added. Pager policy if lock-wait spikes or replication lag > 60s.

maria (db): After canary completes, I'll publish runbook summary + exact tenant order. Will include SQL to revert per-tenant (idempotent) if needed.

jordan (release): Logging final: pinned version set, canary job queued, release-notes published. Tagging @sam for comms once canary is healthy.

sam (product): thanks — will send CS note after canary pass.

deploy-bot: UPDATE: canary completed successfully on tenants [t-101, t-107, t-203, t-305, t-412] at 2023-11-15 02:45 UTC. No errors. Proceeding to gradual backfill per plan.

kevin: moving to 5x rate_delay reduction for low-risk tenants.

ashley (sre): Observability: 0.02% error rate, avg update latency 120ms, replica lag stable. No action.

maria (db): Thanks team — will keep this thread updated for any aborts.

jordan (release): Closing coordination here; follow-up summary will land in the release notes tomorrow.
